codeql_results.message: A Flask app appears to be run in debug mode. This may allow an attacker to run arbitrary code through the debugger.
The full URL of this request depends on a [user-provided value](1).
Cross-site scripting vulnerability due to a [user-provided value](1).

findings.description: Flask application is running in debug mode (app.run(debug=True)), which could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code through the debugger interface.
findings.remediation_description: Disable debug mode in production environments by setting debug=False

findings.description: User-provided subdomain parameter is used to construct a URL without sufficient validation, potentially allowing SSRF attacks despite domain restrictions.
findings.novelty_reason: Standard SSRF pattern with domain validation
findings.remediation_code: Use a whitelist validation library (e.g., validators) instead of string-based domain checking
findings.remediation_description: Replace string-based domain validation with a robust URL parsing and validation library to prevent bypasses

findings.description: User-controlled response content is returned directly to clients without proper sanitization, creating potential XSS vulnerabilities.
findings.novelty_reason: Basic XSS pattern in response handling
findings.remediation_description: Sanitize all user-controlled content before returning it to clients using proper escaping functions

healing_failures.root_cause: XSS vulnerability still present in response handling
Debug mode still enabled in production

report.recommendation: Prioritize fixing the suspected SSRF and debug mode issues first, then address the suspected XSS vulnerability. Implement proper URL validation and disable debug mode in production.
